proof.text:
*(Condition (1) is smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00TB.)* Claim: (1) holds iff there is $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that the ring map $R	o A	o A_g$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] ($A_g$ the localization at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$). For $g\in A$ let $D(g)=\{\mathfrak p:g
otin\mathfrak p\}$, an open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $j_g=\operatorname{Spec}(A	o A_g):\operatorname{Spec}A_g	o\operatorname{Spec}A$; by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] $j_g$ is an open immersion with image $D(g)$, so [def-weil-open-immersion] $j_g=\iota_g\circ u_g$ with $\iota_g$ the inclusion of the open subscheme $D(g)$ and $u_g:\operatorname{Spec}A_g	o D(g)$ an isomorphism; and $\pi\circ j_g=\operatorname{Spec}(R	o A_g)$ by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], i.e. $(\pi|_{D(g)})\circ u_g=\operatorname{Spec}(R	o A_g)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (c) (with $u=u_g$, $v=\mathrm{id}$) $\pi|_{D(g)}$ is smooth iff $\operatorname{Spec}(R	o A_g)$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], iff $R	o A_g$ is a smooth ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. ($\Leftarrow$) If $g
otin\mathfrak q$ and $R	o A_g$ is smooth, $W=D(g)$ is an open containing $\mathfrak q$ with $\pi|_W$ smooth. ($\Rightarrow$) Let $W
i\mathfrak q$ be open with $\pi|_W$ smooth. Its complement is closed, $V(\mathfrak a)=\{\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak a\}$ for an ideal $\mathfrak a$ (Zariski topology), and $\mathfrak q
otin V(\mathfrak a)$ gives $g\in\mathfrak a\setminus\mathfrak q$; then $D(g)\cap V(\mathfrak a)=\emptyset$, so $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (a) applied to $\pi|_W:W	o\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the opens $D(g)\subseteq W$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R$ (the factorization of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] being $\pi|_{D(g)}$), $\pi|_{D(g)}$ is smooth, so $R	o A_g$ is smooth.

proof.text: *(Kernels of small extensions.)* Let $\varphi:B'\to B$ be a small extension, $\mathfrak m'$ the maximal ideal of $B'$ and $I=\ker\varphi$. Since $I$ has length $1$ it is a simple $B'$-module, so $I=B'x$ for any $x\in I\setminus0$ and $b\mapsto bx$ induces $B'/\operatorname{ann}(x)\cong I$ with $\operatorname{ann}(x)$ a maximal ideal, i.e. $\operatorname{ann}(x)=\mathfrak m'$; hence $\mathfrak m'I=0$. As $B\neq0$ (it is local), $I\neq B'$, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m'$ and $I^2\subseteq\mathfrak m'I=0$. Also $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m'$ ($\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$ is a maximal ideal since $\varphi$ is surjective), and $\varphi$ induces an isomorphism $\bar\varphi:B'/I\to B$.

source.place: Algebra, remark after Definition Tag 02HS (definition-small-extension, line 38937): 'Clearly this means that I^2 = 0 and that I = (x) for some x in B' such that m'x = 0'; Lemma Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces) (3)

proof.text: *(Setup for (2) implies (1): a presentation and its conormal map.)* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] there are $n\ge0$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:P\to A$ whose kernel $I$ is a finitely generated ideal; so $A$ is finitely presented over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] $\Omega_{P/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free on $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$, so $A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ is free on $1\otimes\mathrm dx_j$; by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-h1-cotangent-vanishing] $H_1(L_{P/R})=0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-quotient-smooth] (with $A:=R$, $B:=P$, $\mathfrak a:=I$, $C:=A$) gives an exact sequence of $A$-modules $0\to H_1(L_{A/R})\to I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta}A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to\Omega_{A/R}\to0$ with $\delta(f\bmod I^2)=1\otimes\mathrm df$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, second paragraph (presentation S = R[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_m) by Lemma Tag 00FP, the naive cotangent complex I/I^2 -> (+) S dx_j of Section 'netherlander')

proof.text: *(It suffices to split $\delta$ at $\mathfrak q$.)* Suppose the localization $\delta_{\mathfrak q}:(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}\to(A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R})_{\mathfrak q}$ has an $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear left inverse. Localization is exact, so by step 4 $H_1(L_{A/R})_{\mathfrak q}=\ker\delta_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $(\Omega_{A/R})_{\mathfrak q}\cong\operatorname{coker}\delta_{\mathfrak q}$, which is isomorphic to a direct summand (the kernel of the left inverse) of the free module $(A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R})_{\mathfrak q}\cong A_{\mathfrak q}^n$; so it is finitely generated and flat, hence free over the local ring $A_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free]. As $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ (step 4), [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-naive-cotangent-criterion] gives $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $R\to A_g$ smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and (1) holds by step 1. The remaining steps show that (2) implies that $\delta_{\mathfrak q}$ has a left inverse.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, second paragraph: 'It suffices to show that when we localize this complex at q then the map becomes a split injection, see Lemma 07BU (lemma-smooth-at-point)'

proof.text: *(Localizing at $\mathfrak q$.)* Let $\mathfrak q'=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $P$ containing $I$, $C=P_{\mathfrak q'}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak q'C$. $P$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so $C$ is a Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Put $\tilde I=IC\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Since $\alpha(P\setminus\mathfrak q')=A\setminus\mathfrak q$ and localization is exact, $\alpha$ induces $C/\tilde I\cong A_{\mathfrak q}$, carrying $\mathfrak m/\tilde I$ to $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}$, and $\tilde I/\tilde I^2\cong(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$; and $A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}\cong A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\cong(A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R})_{\mathfrak q}$ because $\Omega_{C/R}\cong(\Omega_{P/R})_{\mathfrak q'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization]. Under these isomorphisms $\delta_{\mathfrak q}$ becomes $\delta_C:\tilde I/\tilde I^2\to A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}$, $x\bmod\tilde I^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dx$ ($\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]). It remains to show $\delta_C$ has an $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear left inverse. Note $A$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, second paragraph ('Since localization commutes with taking modules of differentials (Lemma 00RT) ... it suffices to show that the map (equation-target-map) is a split injection'); the detour through S' = P/I^2 is taken in step 11

proof.text: *(The Artinian rings $B'_N\to B_N$.)* For $N\ge1$ put $B'_N=C/(\tilde I^2+\mathfrak m^N)$ and $B_N=C/(\tilde I+\mathfrak m^N)\cong A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^NA_{\mathfrak q}$, let $\pi_N:B'_N\to B_N$ be the quotient map and $I_N=\ker\pi_N=(\tilde I+\mathfrak m^N)/(\tilde I^2+\mathfrak m^N)$; then $I_N^2=0$. Since $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq\tilde I^2+\mathfrak m^N\subseteq\tilde I+\mathfrak m^N\subseteq\mathfrak m$, both are Artinian local rings with maximal ideals the images of $\mathfrak m$, whose $N$-th powers vanish [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local]. Make $B'_N$ an $R$-algebra by $\rho_N:R\to P\to C\to B'_N$ and let $a_N:A\to A_{\mathfrak q}\to B_N$. Then $a_N\circ\varphi_0=\pi_N\circ\rho_N$ (as $\varphi_0=\alpha\circ(R\to P)$ and $C\to B_N$ factors through $C/\tilde I\cong A_{\mathfrak q}$), and $a_N^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{B_N})=\mathfrak q$, because $\mathfrak m_{B_N}=\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^NA_{\mathfrak q}$ and the preimage of $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}$ in $A$ is $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, third paragraph (B'_N = S'_{q'}/(q')^N S'_{q'}, B_N = B'_N/IB'_N = S_q/q^N S_q, 'B'_N is an Artinian local ring since it is the quotient of a local Noetherian ring by a power of its maximal ideal')

proof.text: *(Lifting along a chain of small extensions.)* By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration] there are ideals $0=J_0\subseteq J_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq J_r=I_N$ of $B'_N$ with each $J_i/J_{i-1}$ of length $1$ as a $B'_N$-module. Put $E_i=B'_N/J_i$, so $E_0=B'_N$, $E_r=B_N$. Each $E_i$ is $C/K_i$ for the preimage $K_i$ of $J_i$ in $C$, with $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq K_i\subseteq\tilde I+\mathfrak m^N\subseteq\mathfrak m$, hence an Artinian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local]. The quotient map $\varphi_i:E_{i-1}\to E_i$ is surjective with kernel $J_i/J_{i-1}$, whose $E_{i-1}$-submodules are its $B'_N$-submodules, so it has length $1$ over $E_{i-1}$: $\varphi_i$ is a small extension. Let $\rho^{(i)}:R\to E_i$ be $\rho_N$ followed by the quotient map. Starting from $a^{(r)}=a_N$ (step 7), descending induction gives ring maps $a^{(i)}:A\to E_i$ with $a^{(i)}\circ\varphi_0=\rho^{(i)}$, $\varphi_i\circ a^{(i-1)}=a^{(i)}$ and $(a^{(i)})^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{E_i})=\mathfrak q$: given $a^{(i)}$, condition (2) applied to $\varphi_i$, $\rho=\rho^{(i-1)}$ (note $\varphi_i\circ\rho^{(i-1)}=\rho^{(i)}=a^{(i)}\circ\varphi_0$) and $a=a^{(i)}$ gives $a^{(i-1)}$ with $\varphi_i\circ a^{(i-1)}=a^{(i)}$ and $a^{(i-1)}\circ\varphi_0=\rho^{(i-1)}$; and $(a^{(i-1)})^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{E_{i-1}})=(a^{(i-1)})^{-1}\varphi_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{E_i})=(a^{(i)})^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{E_i})=\mathfrak q$ by step 2. So $s_N=a^{(0)}:A\to B'_N$ satisfies $\pi_N\circ s_N=a_N$ and $s_N\circ\varphi_0=\rho_N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, third paragraph ('Consider a filtration of the kernel I_N ... This gives a sequence of small extensions ... Applying condition (4) successively ...')

proof.text: *(A section of $\pi_N$.)* For $t\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$, $a_N(t)\notin\mathfrak m_{B_N}$, so $s_N(t)\notin\pi_N^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{B_N})=\mathfrak m_{B'_N}$ is a unit; hence $s_N=\tilde s\circ(A\to A_{\mathfrak q})$ for a ring map $\tilde s:A_{\mathfrak q}\to B'_N$. As $s_N(\mathfrak q)\subseteq\pi_N^{-1}(a_N(\mathfrak q))\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B'_N}$, $\tilde s(\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q})\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B'_N}$ and $\tilde s(\mathfrak q^NA_{\mathfrak q})\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B'_N}^N=0$ (step 7). So $\tilde s$ induces $\sigma_N:B_N=A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^NA_{\mathfrak q}\to B'_N$ with $\sigma_N\circ a_N=s_N$. Then $\pi_N\circ\sigma_N\circ a_N=a_N$, and since ring maps out of $B_N$ are determined by their composite with $a_N:A\to A_{\mathfrak q}\to B_N$ (universal property of localization, surjectivity of the quotient map), $\pi_N\circ\sigma_N=\mathrm{id}_{B_N}$. Moreover $\sigma_N$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras ($R\to B_N$ being $\pi_N\circ\rho_N=a_N\circ\varphi_0$): $\sigma_N\circ a_N\circ\varphi_0=s_N\circ\varphi_0=\rho_N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, end of third paragraph ('Clearly the ring map S -> B'_N factors as S -> S_q -> B'_N ... we have shown that for all N the surjection of R-algebras B'_N -> B_N has a splitting')

proof.text: *(Split injectivity at level $N$.)* By step 7 $I_N^2=0$ and by step 9 the surjection of $R$-algebras $\pi_N:B'_N\to B_N$ with kernel $I_N$ has the $R$-algebra right inverse $\sigma_N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-square-zero-section-conormal-retraction] the $B_N$-linear map $\delta_N:I_N\to B_N\otimes_{B'_N}\Omega_{B'_N/R}$, $x\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dx$ ([def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), has a $B_N$-linear left inverse.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, fourth paragraph (the sequence I_N -> B_N (x) Omega_{B'_N/R} -> Omega_{B_N/R} -> 0 of Lemma 00RU is split exact by Lemma 02HP)

proof.text: *(Unwinding modulo $\mathfrak q^k$.)* By [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] (ring $C$, ideal $\mathfrak m$, module $C$, submodule $\tilde I$) there is $c\ge1$ with $\mathfrak m^N\cap\tilde I\subseteq\mathfrak m^{N-c}\tilde I$ for all $N\ge c$. Let $N\ge c+1$, $k=N-c$ (so $1\le k\le N-1$) and $T_k=A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^kA_{\mathfrak q}=C/(\tilde I+\mathfrak m^k)$, a quotient of $B_N$. (a) By the modular law $I_N\cong\tilde I/(\tilde I^2+\mathfrak m^N\cap\tilde I)$, so $T_k\otimes_{B_N}I_N=I_N/\mathfrak m^kI_N\cong\tilde I/(\tilde I^2+\mathfrak m^N\cap\tilde I+\mathfrak m^k\tilde I)=\tilde I/(\tilde I^2+\mathfrak m^k\tilde I)=T_k\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}\tilde I/\tilde I^2$. (b) Let $S'_C=C/\tilde I^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-mod-power-ideal] for $C$, the ideal $\tilde I$ and $n=1$: $A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}\cong A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{S'_C}\Omega_{S'_C/R}$; for $S'_C$, the ideal $\mathfrak mS'_C$ and $n=N-1\ge1$ (note $S'_C/\mathfrak m^NS'_C=B'_N$): $(S'_C/\mathfrak m^{N-1}S'_C)\otimes_{S'_C}\Omega_{S'_C/R}\cong(S'_C/\mathfrak m^{N-1}S'_C)\otimes_{B'_N}\Omega_{B'_N/R}$. As $T_k$ is a quotient of $A_{\mathfrak q}$ and of $S'_C/\mathfrak m^{N-1}S'_C$, tensoring gives $T_k\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}\cong T_k\otimes_{B'_N}\Omega_{B'_N/R}=T_k\otimes_{B_N}(B_N\otimes_{B'_N}\Omega_{B'_N/R})$, all maps sending $1\otimes\mathrm dx$ to $1\otimes\mathrm d\bar x$ ([def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]). (c) Under (a) and (b), $T_k\otimes_{B_N}\delta_N$ and $T_k\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}\delta_C$ both send the class of $x\in\tilde I$ to $1\otimes\mathrm dx$, so they agree. A split injection stays one after tensoring (tensor the left inverse), so by step 10 $T_k\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak q}}\delta_C:(\tilde I/\tilde I^2)/\mathfrak q^k(\tilde I/\tilde I^2)\to(A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R})/\mathfrak q^k(A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R})$ has a left inverse, for every $k\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HT, last paragraph (I_N = I_{q'}/(I_{q'}^2 + (q')^N cap I_{q'}); Artin-Rees, Lemma 00IN; Lemma 02HQ applied to S' and to S'_{q'}; 'a split injection remains a split injection after tensoring with anything')

proof.text: *(Conclusion of (2) implies (1).)* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-split-injection-after-completion] to the Noetherian ring $A_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 6), the ideal $J=\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}$ (the maximal ideal of a local ring, which is its Jacobson radical) and $u=\delta_C$: its source $\tilde I/\tilde I^2$ is finitely generated since $I$ is (step 4), its target $A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}\cong A_{\mathfrak q}^n$ (steps 4 and 6) is finitely generated, and $u_k=T_k\otimes\delta_C$ is a split injection for all $k\ge1$ by step 11. So $\delta_C$, i.e. $\delta_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 6), has a left inverse, and (1) holds by step 5. With step 3, (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2).

title: Reverse implication in the Artinian lifting criterion
statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $\varphi_0:R\to A$ make $A$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $A$. Write $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_0)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A small extension is a surjective homomorphism $\varphi:B^{\prime}\to B$ of nonzero Artinian local commutative rings with kernel of module length one over $B^{\prime}$; write $\mathfrak m_B$ for the maximal ideal of $B$.

Assume: For every small extension $\varphi:B^{\prime}\to B$ and ring homomorphisms $\rho:R\to B^{\prime}$ and $a:A\to B$ such that $a\circ\varphi_0=\varphi\circ\rho$ and $a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak q$, there is a ring homomorphism $a^{\prime}:A\to B^{\prime}$ with $\varphi\circ a^{\prime}=a$ and $a^{\prime}\circ\varphi_0=\rho$.

Then: There is an open subscheme $W$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $\mathfrak q$ with $\pi|_W$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

lean.statement:
theorem artinian_lifting_smooth_on_open_reverse
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (φ₀ : R →+* A) (hfinite : φ₀.FiniteType) (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime] :
    (∀ (B' B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B]
      [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B]
      (φ : B' →+* B), Function.Surjective φ → Module.length B' (RingHom.ker φ) = 1 →
      ∀ (ρ : R →+* B') (a : A →+* B),
        a.comp φ₀ = φ.comp ρ → Ideal.comap a (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) = q →
        ∃ a' : A →+* B', φ.comp a' = a ∧ a'.comp φ₀ = ρ) →
    (∃ W : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens,
      (⟨q, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum A) ∈ W ∧
        Smooth (W.ι ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ₀)))
